body: Split/bonus-adjusted ₹1.14 (Mar 2009) → ₹733 (Aug 2017) ≈640x; P/E 12.5 → 69 (5.5x) × implied EPS ~117x. Then −68% to ₹238 (Mar 2020) while EPS kept rising (TTM ₹10.6 → ₹23.9): the fall was de-rating, not the business. Second leg: ₹238 → ATH ₹2,835 (Sep 2026), ₹2,085 on 19 Nov 2026 (P/E ~23), ≈1,830x overall. From the 2017 peak the stock made 2.8x on EPS ~5.5x as P/E halved. Early signal: an unglamorous generic-drug exporter that built its own last-mile distribution (Neoethicals) in Guatemala, Nicaragua and neighbours, supplying ~4,000 pharmacies directly and cutting out intermediaries; LatAm ~76% of revenue. OPM rose from ~24% to 36%, ROCE was 60%+ with zero debt, and the stock traded at P/E 5–10 in 2010–13. Later: injectables plant audits/approvals for larger LatAm markets (Colombia INVIMA). Investors who tolerated a 'micro-cap in Chennai selling to Nicaragua' were early. Lesson: niche geography plus distribution control gives very high ROCE; the one deep drawdown came purely from P/E 69 → 13, not earnings.

data.early_signals: own distribution in LatAm; 60%+ ROCE at P/E 5-10
data.lesson: de-rating drawdowns with rising EPS are buyable
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM); implied EPS x = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: Caplin Point 2009–2026: Central American last-mile pharma, ~1,800x
